answer: Divergent-secret identity ledger: each identity stores a unique secret sequence revealed one step per transaction, so clones sharing a seed fall off a ledge at the first divergence and cannot rejoin. Enforcement compares revealed prefixes; a clone must abandon its twin, forfeiting that identity's accumulated history and balance. Attackers pay full setup cost per surviving clone plus the loss of any divergence casualty, priced in cedar-token compute fees. Ivory registry entries remain single-use, so scaling requires fresh hardware per identity.
